## How to run cutscene commands

In this skill, `cutscene <command>` is shorthand for:

```bash
node "<this skill's folder>/../cutscene/scripts/cli.mjs" <command>
```

Replace `<this skill's folder>` with the folder this SKILL.md was loaded from. Scripts named `<this skill's folder>/scripts/...` run with plain `node`. Never call the engine through `npx`, and never use cloud commands: Cutscene works on this computer only, and it never renders a final video unless the user asks.

sources.kept: router SKILL.md (as router-guide.md) and its references; plugin installer and its script dropped

cutscene-compose.name: cutscene-compose
cutscene-compose.description: Use when writing or fixing the HTML of a Cutscene video project, once the cutscene skill has the approved brief and look: the composition contract (structure, data-* timing attributes, class="clip", tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules), building a general (non-promo) video scene by scene, and installing ready-made blocks and components from the registry (cutscene catalog / cutscene add). Not the starting point for a new video (that is cutscene). Does NOT choose the look or palette (cutscene-design), author motion (cutscene-animate), mix sound (cutscene-audio), edit footage (cutscene-edit) or render (cutscene-render).

sources.kept: workflow guide, frame-packet script, frame-worker brief

cutscene-animate.name: cutscene-animate
cutscene-animate.description: Use for any motion in a Cutscene video: GSAP timelines, eases and staggers, the runtime adapters (GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations, TypeGPU), atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, motion blur, seek-safe keyframes for zooms, punch-ins and camera moves, auditing choreography with an animation map, kinetic type, and the motion-graphics workflow (lower thirds, charts, maps, 2D logo reveals, news, tweets). Use it when something moves wrong, too fast or too stiff. Does NOT pick the video's look (cutscene-design), make extruded 3D titles or 3D scenes (cutscene-3d) or define the composition contract (cutscene-compose).

sources.kept: workflow guide, agents, category modules, grounding, sample

cutscene-design.name: cutscene-design
cutscene-design.description: Use when deciding how a Cutscene video looks before building it, or when the user says their videos look samey or wants another palette or font: the per-video look system (look.json with palette, background tone, type pair, motion character and texture, generated from the brief and the user's brand colours and fonts, checked for contrast and for being too close to earlier videos), frame presets, palettes, typography, visual styles, beat direction and narration planning, and optional Figma import with the user's own token. Does NOT run the brief and storyboard gates (cutscene), write motion code (cutscene-animate), compose the HTML (cutscene-compose) or make voices (cutscene-voice).

sources.kept: Figma guide (optional, needs the user's FIGMA_TOKEN) and motion verifier
user memory only (remembered preferences and frozen recipes, all local)

cutscene-captions.name: cutscene-captions
cutscene-captions.description: Use to put designed, word-timed captions on a Cutscene video: talking-head or interview footage (caption themes and DNA presets, standard and cinematic modes, typography, safe zones, overflow, occlusion and timing checks, subject matting so words sit behind a person), and word-highlight caption rails for narrated motion graphics with no footage, made from the voice word timings in .cutscene/beats.json (spoken "A I" shown as "AI"). Word timings come from local transcription (cutscene transcribe) or from cutscene-voice. Does NOT cut silences or retakes (cutscene-edit), export plain SRT subtitles (cutscene-edit), make voiceover (cutscene-voice) or render without the user's OK.

cutscene-audio.name: cutscene-audio
cutscene-audio.description: Use for the sound inside a Cutscene composition: placing the user's music and sound effects on the timeline, fade-in/out, crossfades, track gain, volume automation, ducking or carving music under a voiceover, audio effects, diagnosing a muddy mix, and the bundled offline sound-effect library (whoosh, click, impact). Music comes from the user's own files; nothing is fetched from a cloud catalog. Does NOT generate, clone or check voices or transcribe speech (cutscene-voice), and does NOT clean up a recording's own audio, such as hum, background noise or a loudness premix of footage (cutscene-edit).

sources.kept: sound parts only: the SFX library manifest (the Pixabay sound files are not shipped; the sound engine reads them from the installed engine package), ducking script; voice, transcription, HeyGen catalog and image parts dropped

cutscene-render.name: cutscene-render
cutscene-render.description: Use for Cutscene's local command loop once a project exists, and for diagnosing build or render failures: lint, check, snapshot, compare, timeline, preview, doctor, and local render (draft, looks, delivery, batch). Use it when a check fails, a preview is blank or a render errors or stalls. Everything runs on this computer. Not for planning a new video (cutscene). Does NOT publish, upload or render in any cloud, and never renders a final video unless the user asks for it.

cutscene-promo.name: cutscene-promo
cutscene-promo.description: Use for promo-style Cutscene videos made from a product or marketing URL, a GitHub pull request, or a topic or script: product launch, feature reveal and site-tour videos, faceless explainers, and PR-to-video changelog clips. Load it after the cutscene skill (the entry point for every new video) has routed the brief here; each is a gated workflow (brief, script, storyboard, frames, sound, assembly, review). Does NOT edit existing footage (cutscene-edit), make 3D shots (cutscene-3d), or render a final video without the user's OK.

moveSections.heading: ^Voiceover carve$
moveSections.summary: Carve cuts only the bands a voice actually uses out of the music bed, instead of ducking the whole bed, so the music keeps its low end and top while the voice stays clear. The settings live on the bed and name the voices to listen to (as a sidechain does); never put a carve on a voice track. Carve against one group of voice clips, not a list of clip ids. A re-run replaces only its own filters and leaves hand-built effects and lanes alone.

# Source phase (Cutscene)

Runs **only when `shot-plan.json.asset_needs` is non-empty** (the form categories never reach here).

Cutscene has no stock-media search and no image generation, so each asset need is met by one of:

- **User files.** Ask once for the logo, screenshot, photo or clip the plan needs; copy it into `assets/`.
- **A captured site.** `cutscene capture <url> -o ./capture --json`, then pick from `capture/assets/` using `capture/extracted/asset-descriptions.md`.
- **Asset-free.** If neither exists, switch the category to its asset-free layout and note it in `context.log`.

Freeze every file under `assets/` (never hot-link) and write `assets/index.md`: one row per asset with its path, source (user / capture URL) and licence. The design phase reads that index.

thirdParty.intro: Cutscene is built on HyperFrames, an open-source framework by HeyGen (Apache-2.0). Cutscene is independent and not affiliated with HeyGen. The engine itself is the `hyperframes` npm package at the version pinned in `skills/cutscene/engine.json`; it is installed on first use and is not part of this repository. The skills listed below were rebuilt from the HyperFrames skills by `tools/sync-hyperframes.mjs`: copied, renamed and adapted for Cutscene (every adapted file carries an "Adapted from HyperFrames" header). The HyperFrames licence is the Apache License 2.0, the same licence as Cutscene (`LICENSE`).

notSynced.why: ideas only; cutscene-edit is written separately

notSynced.from: media-use (voice, transcription, image, logo, grading parts)
notSynced.why: voice and transcription live in cutscene-voice; HeyGen catalog, image, logo and grading tools are not shipped in v1

bundled.notes: adapted; see the header in each file (Cutscene's own files are listed below)
licence texts kept beside the fonts (OFL-*.txt)

bundled.origin: Google Fonts families via @fontsource (latin subsets): Anton, Audiowide, Baloo 2, Bangers, Bodoni Moda, Caveat, Chakra Petch, Cinzel, Cormorant Garamond, Creepster, Fredoka, Inter, Monoton, Orbitron, Press Start 2P, Rajdhani, Saira Stencil One, Shippori Mincho, Sora, Space Grotesk, Teko, VT323 (SIL OFL 1.1); Permanent Marker, Special Elite (Apache-2.0)
bundled.notes: each family's licence text with its copyright line, as Fontsource ships it, is kept in modes/standard/fonts/licenses/ (OFL-<family>.txt, LICENSE-<family>.txt); see https://github.com/fontsource/font-files

bundled.origin: Hershey vector fonts (Dr. A. V. Hershey, U.S. National Bureau of Standards)
bundled.license: Hershey font use condition (free use; credit the origin)
bundled.notes: single-stroke script fonts used for handwriting reveals

runtime: **GSAP** (GreenSock): loaded by compositions from a pinned CDN URL or provided by the engine. GSAP Standard License (https://gsap.com/standard-license), free for commercial use; not an OSI open-source licence.
**three.js** (MIT), **Lottie** (lottie-web, MIT), **Anime.js** (MIT), **TypeGPU** (MIT): optional runtime adapters documented in cutscene-animate; loaded by a composition only when it uses them.

**Registry blocks and components** installed with `cutscene add` are downloaded from the engine's online registry when the user asks for them; each block keeps its own licence files (for example three.js MIT, GSAP Standard License notices, OFL fonts, Poly Haven CC0 HDRIs).

**Kokoro-82M** (Apache-2.0) voices and the engine's local transcription and cut-out models are downloaded by the engine on first use of `cutscene tts` / `cutscene transcribe` / `cutscene remove-background`, only after the user agrees (`--yes`).

**Sound effects** (19 Pixabay files, Pixabay Content License, https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/): not in this repository, because that licence does not allow sharing them as a standalone library. `skills/cutscene-audio/scripts/sound-engine.mjs` copies them, checksum-checked against `skills/cutscene-audio/sound/sfx/sha256.json`, from the installed engine package (`hyperframes`, which ships them) into a video project's `assets/sfx/` when a video uses them.
**Google Fonts**: compositions may link Google Fonts at render time; families keep their own licences (mostly SIL OFL 1.1).
ideasOnly: **OpenMontage** (calesthio/OpenMontage, AGPL-3.0): pipeline catalogue and routing studied for ideas; no code or text copied.
**eden-motion** (no licence): the HyperFrames + Blender plate idea only; nothing copied.
**VoiceStudio** (AGPL-3.0): used only over its local API when the user has it; nothing copied.
